## Comment from optinosis team: Cerebras GLM-4.7 also affected

We hit this exact bug with the **Cerebras Z.AI GLM-4.7** model on OpenCode v1.14.33. Our internal issue: https://github.com/optinosis/optinosis/issues/2229

We confirmed that:

- Three complete fix PRs exist (#24250, #24428, #24895) but **none were merged**
- The bug affects **any** OpenAI-compatible provider that returns `reasoning_content` but doesn't accept it as input - not just DeepSeek
- `implementsReasoning: false` (an undocumented field) does nothing - it's a silent no-op
- The interleaved transform is internal to the SDK pipeline, not configurable via `.opencode/opencode.json`

Our temporary workaround is to disable reasoning (`reasoning_effort: none`), but that significantly degrades model quality for complex tasks (~20-30% drop for architecture/design, ~5% for simple tasks).

We believe a merge of any one of the three PRs - particularly #24250 which is the most comprehensive (3-layer fix covering auto-enable interleaved, dynamic SDK key, and unconditional reasoning injection for all assistant messages) - would resolve this for Cerebras GLM-4.7 and all other affected providers.

Could you review one of these? Happy to provide additional testing or reproductions.

Confirming this with **MCP tool calls** as well, not just `write` / `apply_patch`.

Setup: macOS, opencode `1.14.33`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` with `effort: high`, custom subagent invoked via `task`.

Pattern: subagent completes useful work (git commit succeeded, files written), then calls `engram_mem_save` (MCP tool, ~5-15KB markdown payload) as the last action. The tool call hangs forever, UI shows it in flight, no abort, 6+ minutes idle and counting.

Diagnostic from `ps` and `lsof` on the MCP child process while stuck:

```
PID    ELAPSED STAT WCHAN
96402  02:48   S+   -

lsof -p 96402 | grep PIPE
engram 96402 ... 6 PIPE 16384 -> ...
engram 96402 ... 7 PIPE 16384 -> ...
```

The MCP child is in `S+` (foreground sleep) on the stdin pipe, waiting for input that never arrives. The FDs are 16KB pipes (default macOS pipe buffer). That number lines up with the "large file" workarounds in this thread: payloads above 16KB risk partial writes that deadlock without a timeout.

Workaround that worked here: split the \`mem_save\` content. Instead of one large save at end of phase, save smaller deltas during the run.

Related: #21250 (subagent runs stall after last completed tool), #25360 (no timeout on tool execution).
